data.name: Jawaharlal
data.gender_notes: Jawaharlal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jawaharlal is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Jaya' (victory) and 'Hari' (God), and 'Rama' (pleasing) and 'Lalita' (playful). It symbolizes the gentle, compassionate, and brave qualities of the Hindu gods Jaya and Hari. The name Jawaharlal carries the meaning “Gentle, Compassionate, and Brave” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Jawaharlal usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, compassionate, and brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Jawaharlal is a spiritual name that represents the qualities of courage, leadership, and devotion to the Hindu gods. It is believed to bring success and victory in life, and to inspire a deep sense of compassion and kindness towards others.
data.etymology: Jawaharlal belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle, Compassionate, and Brave.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jawaharlal total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
